title: When circular RNAs meet the genome: CiR-loops as chromatin regulators and disease drivers.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the open-access full text (84 KB) and the Europe PMC supplementary package (0.63 MB). The supplement holds only 12 image files (figures 1-5 plus a graphical abstract, as .jpg and .gif) and zero data tables. The data availability statement reads verbatim: 'No primary research results or new data were generated as part of this review.' Grepped the entire full text for accessions (GSE, SRP, PRJ, E-MTAB), Zenodo/Dryad/figshare/GitHub links: none found. Europe PMC flags confirm hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N. A Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology described (circular RNAs hybridising with genomic DNA to form R-loops, their formation and resolution mechanisms, disease links) is entirely narrative review text citing other people's experiments. The only data resources it names in passing are R-loopBase and DRIP-seq (a sequencing assay that maps DNA-RNA hybrids), both belonging to other publications.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset at all. This is a narrative review; its data availability statement states no new data were generated, and the only supplementary files are the paper's own figure images. Nothing to download, so A1 fails outright.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table, so no label column anywhere. Any ciR-loop project would require building the label from scratch by joining third-party R-loop mapping data (DRIP-seq peaks) to circular RNA annotations from a separate database, which is exactly the 'label must be constructed' failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences, coordinates or features are distributed with the paper; every input would have to be assembled from external resources.

a4_units_stated.note: No measurements are reported in any machine-readable form, so units are not applicable.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero rows. No data file exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, because there is nothing to load. Passing here is meaningless.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts exist to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists. Any label would come from someone else's peak calls or, worse, from existing R-loop predictors such as deepRloopPre, which would be distilling another model rather than learning biology.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper is a literature review that generated and deposited no data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA and circular RNA sequence to predict which genomic sites form circular-RNA-derived R-loops.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need genomic windows labelled as R-loop-forming or not, with each window's sequence plus whether a circular RNA overlaps it. None of this is in the paper; the number of examples is unknown and would depend entirely on third-party DRIP-seq (a sequencing assay that maps DNA-RNA hybrids) datasets.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a genomic site carries a ciR-loop, a three-stranded structure in which a circular RNA pairs with one DNA strand and displaces the other. The true answer would come from other labs' R-loop sequencing peak calls, not from this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chromatin and genome-stability researchers would want a map of which loci are at risk from these unusually hard-to-resolve structures, but this review supplies none of the measurements needed to build it.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The nearest idea - predicting ciR-loop-forming loci from sequence - would have to be built entirely from other publications' DRIP-seq peaks and circular RNA catalogues (circAtlas, CIRCpedia), and the general R-loop prediction task is already occupied by deepRloopPre and DeepER. If that idea is ever pursued, start from an actual R-loop mapping paper or from R-loopBase, not from this review.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; there is no dataset, so every compute figure is undefined.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement: 'No primary research results or new data were generated as part of this review.' That one line, plus seeing that the supplement is 12 figure images, kills it in two minutes.

verdict_reason: Narrative review with no data: the availability statement says no new data were generated, the supplement contains only figure images, and no accessions or repository links appear anywhere in the full text. Part A1 fails, and A2/A3 would fail too since any ciR-loop label would have to be constructed from other papers' R-loop sequencing data.
